messages:
alex: heads up — post-nightly firmware rollout in us-west-2 a subset of racks flipped boot flags at the BMC/UEFI layer. seeing provisioning stalls and GPU pools reporting low capacity. :(
maria: how many racks/nodes affected? impact on live clusters?
alex: rough numbers: 12 racks, ~48 nodes, ~384 GPUs behind those nodes. about half are failing PXE or timing out during kexec. some show "Secure Boot: Enabled" where previously disabled.
sam: possible this is the rollout toggling the UEFI variable on flash. can we grab a serial log from one of the failing nodes?
kevin: NTP skew + DHCP lease churn may be amplifying the timeout window. saw ARP storms on the outboard switch concurrently.
alex: attaching quick logs from console (trimmed):
```
[ 0.000000] UEFI: SecureBoot = 1
[ 0.123456] IPMI: got firmware update notif
[ 1.234567] network: pxeboot timeout after 90s
kexec: exit status 1
```
ops-bot: alert: firmware-rollout-usw2 -> 12 racks reported bootflag change (auto-tagged). Incident severity: P2.
lucy-oncall: pinging infra leads, will spin a mitigation call. if boot flags are flipping we may need a staged rollback and hotfix to the flashing job.
maria: immediate mitigation: can we exclude racks from next staging run and mark them as quarantined so autoscaler avoids them?
alex: put a quick tag on the affected racks and set the cloud-provisioner to ignore them: `rackctl tag add --id rack-{id} flaky-firmware-1761118`
sam: runbook option A = remote re-flash with corrected nvram defaults. option B = boot with recovery image that ignores secureboot. re-flash has risk of bricking if power drops.
kevin: cost/ops note: if we quarantine and drain, we'll spill load to other regions. projected extra egress/spot usage ~$6k/day until repaired. ops team ok?
lucy-oncall: prioritize minimizing customer-visible throttles. start quarantine + soak then attempt recovery on 2 racks as canary.
alex: started quarantine tags on 12 racks. kicked drain for affected nodes. autoscaler scale-up triggered in eu-west-1 and us-central which mitigates latency but increases cost.
deploy-bot: firmware-deploy job #7865: rollback flag set -> partial rollback queued for racks: r-349,r-351.
maria: can eng-infra ops script adjust batching to avoid toggling nvram variables? we should add a safelist check.
sam: agree — will add a validation before flashing: read nvram, only write if value differs AND host is in maintenance window. patch incoming.
kevin: captured pcap snippet showing DHCP OFFER retransmits ~3s interval during PXE which lines up with kexec timeouts. switching to longer DHCP lease timeout temporarily might reduce timeouts.
lucy-oncall: action list: 1) quarantine + drain (done), 2) rollback flashing on 2 canary racks (in progress), 3) add nvram guard to flashing job (sam), 4) increase pxeboot timeout to 180s for affected pools (kevin), 5) postmortem + cost impact estimate (maria).
maria: I'll start a quick cost calc and document in ops runbook. initial estimate: $4.2k/day extra across regions with current spill.
alex: can confirm we have serial access for all affected nodes; starting remote serial reflash on canary r-349 now.
sam: running remote toolchain: `oobctl flash --host r-349-node-02 --image usw2/bmc-v2.1.3 --safe-write`
ops-bot: oob session established for r-349-node-02.
kevin: monitoring GPU pool: pool-usw2-gpu1 available GPUs now 230 -> 198 after drains. keep an eye on queue latency.
alex: canary reflash succeeded on r-349 (nvram preserved, secureboot remains disabled). will roll to second canary r-351 if stable for 10m.
lucy-oncall: good sign. if second canary holds, proceed with staged rollback across remaining racks in groups of 3. maintain 5m observation windows.
maria: noted for postmortem: add variance test for bootflag flip during staging and include explicit 'do-not-toggle-secboot' toggle for flash jobs.
sam: patch PR opened: add nvram-check + maintenance-window enforcement to firmware-stager (#4928).
deploy-bot: PR #4928 merged to staging, scheduled for next canary build.
alex: wrap-up: quarantine tagging and drains prevented major customer impact, canary rollback succeeded, cost hit accepted for now. will follow up with full postmortem and RCA timeline. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: leaving notes in cluster runbook about DHCP timeout tuning and monitoring thresholds.
maria: assigning postmortem lead to @maria. deadline EOD tomorrow.
lucy-oncall: will keep monitoring, reopen if rollouts resurface. :eyes:
